PIB Backgrounder

India’s Infrastructure Transformation: From Connectivity to Capacity

प्रविष्टि तिथि:
12 AUG 2026 6:48PM by PIB Delhi

 Building the Foundation of Growth

India’s infrastructure landscape has undergone a major transformation over the past 12 years. From transport and logistics to housing and water, infrastructure development has moved towards integrated planning and large-scale expansion. This has strengthened connectivity, improved access to essential services and created the foundations for sustained economic growth. Public capital expenditure has risen from about
₹2 lakh crore in FY 2014–15 to ₹12.2 lakh crore in FY 2026–27
, supporting this advancement.

 A New Era of Rail Mobility

Indian Railways is moving towards faster, safer and more modern mobility. Electrification, advanced safety systems, high-speed rail and new-generation trains are reshaping the rail network.

Railway budget increased from
₹32,000 crore in 2014–15 to ₹2.78 lakh crore in FY2026–27.

Rail electrification increased from about 20% before 2014 to
99.6% by July 2026
.

162 Vande Bharat
,
2 Vande Bharat Sleeper
Services and
72 Amrit Bharat
 services have improved connectivity and travel experience.

The
Kavach Version 4.0
has been commissioned on
2,633 route km as of July 2026
.

The Mumbai–Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail Corridor
 is being developed over a
508 km
 route with a design speed of
350 kmph
.

Of the
 1,340 stations
identified under the
Amrit Bharat Station Scheme
, redevelopment has been completed for
261 stations
as on 18 July 2026.

First indigenously developed
Hydrogen Fuel Cell Trainset
 has been launched in July 2026. It is a 10-coach train with capacity for around
2,600 passengers
, running on the Jind–Sonipat section. It generates its own electricity onboard with water vapour and heat as the only by-product.






Roads and Highways
Connecting India

A wider and more capable road network is bringing regions closer. The expansion of National Highways, rural roads and major corridors is enabling smoother movement of people and goods.

India has the world’s second-largest road network at
63.73 lakh km
.

Length of national highways
increased by about 61%,
 from
91,287 km in FY 14 to 1,46,572 km in March 2026
.

The length of four-lane and above national highways
increased from 18,371 km in 2014 to 45,516 km.

The length of roads increased from
3.86 lakh km during 2000–2014 to 4.11 lakh km during 2014–2026 under Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana.
Since September 2024, PMGSY-IV has been launched with an objective to provide connectivity to 25,000 unconnected habitations by the year 2029.

Under Bharatmala,
22,590 km
 of roads have been completed till
31 March 2026
.


Bridges and Tunnels: Engineering New Frontiers

Engineering breakthroughs are overcoming some of India’s most demanding geographical challenges. These projects are opening new routes across difficult terrain.

Chenab Bridge (2025):
 World's highest railway arch bridge, standing 359 m above the Chenab River; 1,315 m steel structure strengthening Jammu–Srinagar connectivity.

Anji Khad Bridge (2025):
 India's first cable-stayed railway bridge, in Jammu & Kashmir.

Pamban Bridge (2025):
 India's first vertical-lift railway sea bridge, connecting Rameswaram to the mainland; 2.07 km with a 72.5 m vertical lift span.

Z-Morh/Sonamarg Tunnel (2025):
 12 km tunnel providing all-weather access through avalanche-prone terrain in J&K, improving movement towards Ladakh.

Sudarshan Setu (2024):
 2.32 km bridge connecting Okha with Beyt Dwarka, Gujarat.

Atal Tunnel (2020):
 9.02 km — world's longest highway tunnel above 10,000 feet, connecting Manali and Lahaul-Spiti.

Dr. Syama Prasad Mukherjee Tunnel (2017):
 9 km all-weather tunnel between Jammu and Srinagar, cutting travel time by ~2 hours.

 Civil Aviation and Regional Air Access

Air connectivity is reaching more cities, towns and remote regions. The expansion of airports, UDAN routes and digital passenger services is making flying more accessible across the country.

UDAN
 connected
95 airports, heliports, and water aerodromes
 through
679 routes
, benefiting over
1.68 crore passengers
 as on 15 July 2026.

Operational airports increased from
74 in 2014
 to
165 in July 2026
.

25 greenfield airports
 have been approved after 2014.

Digi Yatra
 is active at
38 airports. The app has enabled over 10 crore seamless journeys with over 2.4 crore downloads
.

Modified UDAN
 has been approved in March 2026 for FY 2026–27 to FY 2035–36 with an outlay of
₹28,840 crore
, envisioning
100 new airports and 200 modern helipads
 to strengthen last-mile regional air connectivity.


Metro: The Rise of Mass Urban Transit

India’s urban mobility network is expanding in scale and scope. Metro connectivity now spans more cities, while innovative systems are opening new possibilities for urban transport.

Metro network expanded from
248 km in 2014
 to over
1,155 km in 2026
.

Cities with metro connectivity increased from
5 to 26
, while daily ridership crossed
1.15 crore passengers
.

Kolkata operationalised
 India’s first underwater metro tunnel
in 2024.

Kochi operationalised
India’s first Water Metro
system with the first boat launched in December 2021.


India’s Maritime Momentum

India is strengthening its maritime backbone to support a growing economy and expanding trade. Investments in ports, waterways and maritime infrastructure are creating a more capable and connected ecosystem.

Major ports’ cargo handling capacity
 nearly doubled from
873 MMTPA in 2014
 to
1,728 MMTPA in 2026
.

Vessel turnaround time
 improved from
94 hours
 to
48.8 hours in 2025-26
.

Major ports collectively handled 915.17 MT of cargo during FY 2025-26,
 increasing from
581 MT in FY 2014-15
.

The
Sagarmala Programme
 strengthened port-led development, coastal connectivity, and logistics integration.

National waterways
 increased from
5 in 2014 to 111 in 2026
, of which
32 are operational
.

India became the world's No. 1 ship-recycling nation in 2025
, with its global share rising from 30.1% (2024) to
35.4% (2025)
 — recycling
2.99 million gross tons (GT)
, up nearly 60% from 1.86
million GT in 2024.

Jawaharlal Nehru Port ranked
22
nd

as per the Container Port Performance Index (CPPI) 2025, published by the World Bank.


Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool (BMIP)
 has been launched on 12 May 2026. It is a USD 1.5 billion domestic insurance pool with a sovereign guarantee of USD 1.4 billion (₹12,980 crore), covering Hull & Machinery, Cargo, Protection and Indemnity, and War risk for Indian-flagged/controlled vessels. As on 29th July 2026, a total of
1608 policies
 covering Cargo War risks and Hull War risks have been issued under the Pool.


Strengthening Logistics and Industrial Capacity

Infrastructure is increasingly being planned as an interconnected network supporting industry and trade. From GatiShakti to industrial corridors, the focus is on improving coordination, efficiency and manufacturing capacity.

PM GatiShakti National Master Plan
 integrated infrastructure planning across
58 Ministries and Departments
 using over
3,291 data layers
.

As on 11 August 2026,
396 infrastructure projects
 with a total estimated cost of about ₹18.66 Lakh Crore have been evaluated through the Network Planning Group mechanism. Out of these, 256 projects have been sanctioned and
198 projects
 are under implementation.

The
National Logistics Policy
 has strengthened multimodal logistics efficiency and supply chain integration.

PRAGATI
 reviewed
382 projects
 worth over
₹85 lakh crore
 and resolved
2,958 issues
.

Over
4,220 industrial parks
 are mapped on the
India Industrial Land Bank (IILB)
.

272 plug-and-play industrial parks
 are operational across the country.

20 industrial smart cities
 have been approved across
7 industrial corridors
.

The
BHAVYA
scheme

has been approved in March 2026 to develop
100 new plug-and-play industrial parks
.

BHAVYA Rasayan Scheme
 has been approved on 24 July 2026, with an outlay of
₹3,030 crore
. The scheme will be implemented over five years, from FY2026–27 to FY2030–31.

7 Pradhan Mantri MITRA Parks
have been proposed to strengthen the manufacturing ecosystem.


Water, Housing and Urban Development

The infrastructure push extends directly to people’s homes and everyday needs. From tap-water access and affordable housing to urban renewal, these efforts are shaping better living conditions across rural and urban India.

Under
Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM)
, rural tap water coverage increased from
3.23 crore
in 2019 to around
15.91 crore households
 as on 10
th
 August 2026.

JJM 2.0
 has been approved in March 2026. The mission has been extended to December 2028, with an enhanced outlay of
₹8.69 lakh crore
.

Under
Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban (PMAY-U)
,
99.25 lakh houses
 have been completed as on 12 August 2026. Around
96% of houses
 under
PMAY-U 2.0
 are allotted to women.

Under
Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Grameen (PMAY-G), out of the 3.91 crore houses
sanctioned,
3.13 crore
houses have been

completed as on 12 August 2026.  Nearly
75%
 of the houses sanctioned under PMAY-G are either in the name of women or under joint ownership.

The
SWAMIH Fund
launched in 2019 delivered over
63,000 homes
, benefiting around
2.52 lakh people
 as of June 2026.

Under
AMRUT and AMRUT 2.0
, projects worth about
₹2.79 lakh crore
 have been sanctioned since 2015.

Under Smart Cities Mission, a total of
7,790 projects
 worth
₹1,56,257 crore
 have been completed as of March 2026.

Infrastructure for a Stronger, Future-Ready India

India’s infrastructure journey reflects a decisive shift in the scale and ambition of national development. The focus has moved towards building resilient, high-capacity systems that not only support a fast-growing economy today but also anticipate the needs of tomorrow. Collectively, these initiatives are strengthening the foundation for a more efficient, inclusive, and future-ready India.
